title: Resident Evil
review: A simple, linear story like a videogame, missing the qualities you'd typically want from a film. It's excellent as a thrill ride, and it does feel like you're watching Austin Abrams play the game, but I have no desire to watch it again any time soon. There's nothing to it except the fun violence from moment to moment. I enjoyed how much reverence it had for the games, and also for {The Evil Dead 2}. Highly grotesque, but in a supernatural and computer animated way, that doesn't hit me as hard as more grounded and practical gore. Sure it goes off the rails towards the end, pivoting from horror to comedy, but what else can you do? The games do it. Maybe 8 is harsh, but I'm anticipating this being a singular experience for me, unlike {Weapons} which I find very rewatchable. And based on the way he talks about it in all the podcast appearances he's doing, I think Zach Cregger wanted to bang out a cheeky 8/10 from the start.
spoilers: It forgets about its own story after the voice note scene, but that's ok, because if that note is ever found, that's the end of his story anyway. The ending in particular was the most fun it could have been. Nobody is an established character from the game, and nobody matters, so why not kill them all? Why not make it a crazy origin story for that boss monster from {Resident Evil 2}?
